key_insight: DepthMaster aims to unify monocular depth estimation across both standard perspective images and 360° panoramic images, so one model can produce metric depth in very different viewing geometries. The core breakthrough is treating these camera types as a shared depth problem rather than separate tasks.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of generalized metric depth estimation for both narrow field-of-view perspective images and panoramic images. Existing methods are often camera-specific and fail to transfer well because perspective and panoramic images have fundamentally different geometry and projection characteristics.
method: Designs a unified monocular depth estimation framework that works for both perspective and panoramic inputs.
Accounts for geometric discrepancies between camera types so the model can learn a shared representation of depth.
Targets metric depth prediction that generalizes across diverse real-world settings instead of being limited to a single camera domain.
impact: This matters for practitioners because it reduces the need to maintain separate depth models for different cameras and environments. A unified approach can simplify deployment in robotics, AR/VR, mapping, and indoor/outdoor vision systems where camera types vary.

paper_title: DepthMaster: Unified Monocular Depth Estimation for Perspective and Panoramic Images
